Judgment
. Heard. Rule.
Rule made returnable forthwith.
Heard finally by consent of the learned Counsel for both sides.

2. Present Application is preferred for quashing and setting aside the Criminal Complaint bearing Regular Criminal Case No. 122/2024 arising out of Crime No. 128/2020 and Chargesheet No.
121/2024 dated 2/7/2024 registered with Police Station, Katol, District Nagpur for the offence punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 328 of Indian Penal Code (for short, 'IPC') read with Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 30(2)(a) and 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'FSS Act').
3.

The prosecution case in brief is that, the Respondent No.2/Complainant, who was the Food Safety Officer, Nagpur, received a phone call from the Police Station, Katol informing that Police Officer has seized four wheeler vehicle bearing registration No. MH-31-CQ-2980 which was carrying contraband articles as declared by the State Government in view of Notification dated 19/7/2019.
Accordingly, the contraband articles were seized by the Police after taking search of the vehicle along with panchas.

4. It is further case of the prosecution that after receipt of such 3/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt information Complainant along with panchas went to the Police Station, Katol and taken search of the vehicle along with panchas, wherein the Complainant found Gutkha, which is declared as contraband article by the State Government.
Thereafter the Complainant has taken the sample of the said contraband article in presence of panchas and sent the same to the Food and Drugs Administrations Laboratory, Nagpur on 30/10/2019.

entities.text: Food and Drugs Administrations Laboratory, Nagpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, Complainant received the Report of Food Analyst, Food and Drugs Administrations Laboratory, Nagpur dated 7/12/2019, wherein it is mentioned that the sample of Gutkha is a contraband article in view of the Notification dated 19/7/2019 issued by the State Government under Section 30(2) (a) of FSS Act.

entities.text: Food and Drugs Administrations Laboratory, Nagpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On the basis of above report, an offence came to be registered against the Applicants.
5. It is the submission of Applicant that Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 is a separate enactment, and therefore, provisions of IPC is not applicable.

It is further stated that under FSS Act an independent procedure for search, seizure, sampling and consent of the Commissioner prior to lodging prosecution are the mandatory requirement, but in violation of the same, offence is registered against them.
Hence, same deserves to be quashed and set aside.
In support of the submission, Applicants have relied upon the following Judgments.

(i) Ram Nath V/s State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, (2024) 3 Supreme Court Cases 502;
Anil S/O Bhimrao Barange And Another vs State Of Mah., Thr. P.S.O. Ps Katol, ... on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32077928/
2 (ii) Sharat Babu Digumarti V/s Government of NCT of Delhi, AIR 2017 Supreme Court 150; and (iii) Joseph Kurian Philip Jose V/s State of Kerala, (1994) 6 Supreme Court Cases 535.
7.

entities.text: Ram Nath V/s State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, (2024) 3 Supreme Court Cases 502
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sharat Babu Digumarti V/s Government of NCT of Delhi, AIR 2017 Supreme Court 150
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Joseph Kurian Philip Jose V/s State of Kerala, (1994) 6 Supreme Court Cases 535
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned APP submitted that although the Act of 2006 is a special law and Indian Penal Code is a general law, there is no bar to apply the provisions of Indian Penal Code for deterrent action against the Applicants in order to prevent them from committing further offence.
Hence, in the public interest and for proper investigation, the offence under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 328 of IPC are registered against the Applicants.
8. In the background of above submissions made by the learned Counsel for both sides, I have perused the record as well as case laws which are cited before this Court.

9. On going through the First Information Report and Chargesheet, it 5/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt is clear that main allegation against the present Applicants is that as per the Notification dated 19/7/2019 the State Government has banned the tobacco as well as scented tobacco in the State of Maharashtra.

As such, in violation of the said Notification, the Applicants were carrying Panmasala,
Gutkha etc. from the State of Madhya Pradesh to State of Maharashtra, and therefore, the offence was registered against the present Applicants.

10. The learned Counsel for Applicants then pointed out from the Notification dated 19/7/2019 that tobacco which was manufactured in the nature of chewing tobacco with additives is defined as "food" under the FSS Act.
Therefore, he has made a submission that once it is defined as a "food", it cannot be considered as "an adulterous food or article" in the matter.

11. The perusal of Sections 272, 273 and 328 of IPC indicates that the offence can be made out against the accused where the article involved was food or drink meant to be consumed by live persons and if it is found that the accused has adulterated it and such adulteration rendered it noxious as food or drink and that the accused at the time of such adulteration intended to sell such article as food or drink or knew it to be likely that such article would be sold as a food or drink.
However, in the present case, according to the Applicants, ingredients of Sections 272 and 273 of IPC are not satisfied.
So 6/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt also there is no case of such a nature, either in the Complaint or in the Chargesheet.
Therefore, prosecuting the Applicants for such offences is not permissible in the matter.

12. The Applicants further stated that as per Section 328 of IPC, the offence is made out, only in the circumstances, where the prosecution proved that substance in question is a poison, or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug etc., and further accused administered the substance to the complainant or caused complainant to take such substance with intent to cause hurt or knowing it to be likely that he was thereby caused hurt or with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of an offence.
However, in the present case, these ingredients are not prima facie established on record after going through the First Information Report as well as Chargesheet.

Anil S/O Bhimrao Barange And Another vs State Of Mah., Thr. P.S.O. Ps Katol, ... on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32077928/
3 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned Counsel for Applicants then pointed out the provisions of the Cigarettes and Order Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce,
Production, supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (for short, 'the Act of 2003'), whereby the legislature has, in its Statement of Objects and Reasons, held that tobacco is universally regarded as one of the major public health hazards and it is responsible directly or indirectly to the health of the citizens.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and Order Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce,
Production, supply and Distribution) Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the need for a 7/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt comprehensive legislation to prohibit advertising and regulation of production, supply and distribution of cigarettes and tobacco products was recommended by the Parliamentary Committee.

Accordingly, for the effective implementation the provisions have been proposed with an objective to reduce the exposure of people to tobacco smoke and to prevent the sale of tobacco products to minors and to protect them from becoming victims of misleading advertisements.
As such, it is the submission of the Applicants that by the Act of 2003, Parliament did not totally banned the manufacture of tobacco or scented tobacco products.

The provisions of the said Act only prohibits the sale of cigarette and tobacco products to the person below the age of 18 years and by the said Act only the care has to be taken while issuing advertisement for the product of tobacco and cigarette.

14. In the light of this submission, learned Counsel for the Applicants pointed out that the Applicants cannot be prosecuted under the provisions of Indian Penal Code even in a case if it is found that they were carrying the banned articles in violation of Notification issued by the State Government.

15. In support of the submission learned Counsel for Applicants has strongly relied upon the Judgment of Ram Nath (supra), wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the provisions of the Act of 2006 are exhaustive 8/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt and substantive for dealing with the offences concerning unsafe food. Section 89 of the Act of 2006
clearly gives overriding effect to the provisions of the Act of 2006 over any other law insofar as the law applies to the aspects of food in the field covered by the Act of 2006.
It is also held that the provisions under Section 59 of the Act of 2006 is more stringent than the other provisions.

Therefore, considering the entire legal position,
the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that by virtue of Sections 89 and 59 of the Act of 2006, it overrides the provisions of Sections 272 and 273 of IPC, and hence, the prosecution under the provisions of Indian Penal Code was held illegal.
16.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Sharat Babu Digumarti (supra) also laid down the law that if legislation has enacted certain Act with special provisions having the overriding effect to cover the criminal act, the same will prevail over the general act.

In this regard paragraph No.32 of the said Judgment would be relevant to reproduce here, which is as under :
"32.
The aforesaid passage clearly shows that if legislative intendment is discernible that a latter enactment shall prevail, the same is to be interpreted in accord with the said intention.
We have already referred to the scheme of the IT Act and how obscenity pertaining to electronic record falls under the scheme of the Act.
We have also referred to Sections 79 and 81 of the IT Act.
Once the special provisions having the overriding effect do cover a criminal act and the offender, he gets out of the net of the IPC and in this case, Section 292.

Anil S/O Bhimrao Barange And Another vs State Of Mah., Thr. P.S.O. Ps Katol, ... on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32077928/
4 9/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt

entities.text: Anil S/O Bhimrao Barange And Another vs State Of Mah., Thr. P.S.O. Ps Katol
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: it is apt to note here that electronic forms of transmission is covered by the IT Act, which is a special law.
It is settled position in law that a special law shall prevail over the general and prior laws.

When the Act in various provisions deals with obscenity in electronic form, it covers the offence under Section 292 IPC."
17.

The learned Counsel for Applicants has further relied upon the Judgment of Joseph Kurian Philip Jose (supra), wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that to prove the offence under Section 328 of IPC the prosecution is required to prove that the substance in question was a poison,
or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug etc., that the accused administered the substance to the complainant or caused the complainant to take such substance with intent to cause hurt or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby cause hurt, or with the intention to commit or facilitate the commission of an offence.
Hence, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that the accused was directly responsible for administering poison etc. or causing it to be taken by any person, through another.

18. In the light of the submission of the Applicants, the submission made by the learned APP is that in the present matter considering the offence committed by the Applicants, prosecution has already implicated the Applicants under the provisions of the Act of 2006.

However, Section 328 of 10/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt Indian Penal Code is required to be considered in the matter, because tobacco and the materials, which Applicants were carrying, was prohibited in the State of Maharashtra.
Therefore, carrying of such material in the State of Maharashtra was certainly with intention to cause hurt to the persons at large, and therefore, prohibitory action has been taken in the matter.

Hence, considering the quantity which was seized from the vehicle of the Applicants,
offence under Section 328 of IPC is attracted in the facts and circumstances of the matter.
19. The learned APP did not dispute about the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Ram Nath (supra) as well as overriding effect of Section 89 of the Act of 2006.
There is no satisfactory explanation from the learned APP as to how the provisions of Indian Penal Code are attracted when the Applicants are charged with provisions of FSS Act in the matter.
Hence, the learned APP could not justify the applicability of the provisions of Indian Penal Code in the facts of the present case.

20. In the light of above discussion, I am of the opinion that considering the provisions of special enactment which is having overriding effect, continuing the prosecution against the provisions of IPC would not be 11/12 Judg.APL.252.2020.odt proper.

Hence offence registered under Section 188,
272, 273 and 328 of IPC needs to be quashed and set aside.

21. It is pertinent to note that in addition to this Complaint it is under challenge by way of present Application that Food Safety Officer has lodged independent complaint against the present Applicants under the provisions of FSS Act.
The bare perusal of the said complaint demonstrates the fact that on the basis of same incident the complaint has been lodged under the same provisions of the FSS Act.
In view of this, in my opinion, it will not be proper to make any comment on the provisions under which the offence is registered in the matter.

Anil S/O Bhimrao Barange And Another vs State Of Mah., Thr. P.S.O. Ps Katol, ... on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32077928/

sentences.text:
In my opinion, in view of filing of the independent complaint by the Food Safety Officer, Regular Criminal Case No. 122/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 30(2)(a)
and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is liable to be quashed and set aside with liberty to the Food Safety Officer to continue the private Complaint No. 9698/2020 in accordance with law which is already initiated in the matter.
Hence, for the reasons stated above, I proceed to pass following order.
ORDER 1. Criminal Application is allowed.

The offence punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 328 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 30(2)(a) and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in Regular Criminal Case No. 122/2024, which is pending on the file of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Katol, District Nagpur is hereby quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Katol, District Nagpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The Food Safety Officer is permitted to proceed with Misc. Criminal Case No. 9698/2020 for the offences registered under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards &
Food Additives) Regulation, 2011, which is pending before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Nagpur.

Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards &
Food Additives) Regulation, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Rule is made absolute in above terms.
No order as to costs.
